tldr: Most tourists need NO visa for a short stay — but you almost always need the free e-Arrival Card.
K-ETA is temporarily waived for 22 countries through 31 Dec 2026; it returns 1 Jan 2027.
If you DO need K-ETA: apply only at k-eta.go.kr, ₩10,000, valid 3 years, at least 72h before you fly.

documents.title: The 3 documents, in plain English
documents.intro: Entering Korea can involve up to three separate things. Most short-term tourists only deal with one or two of them. Here is what each one actually is:

cards.name: Tourist Visa
cards.who: Only nationalities NOT on the visa-free list
cards.what: A visa sticker/label you get from a Korean embassy before you travel.

cards.name: K-ETA
cards.what: An electronic travel authorization linked to your passport. Not a visa — it's permission to board.

cards.name: e-Arrival Card
cards.what: A digital entry/customs declaration that replaced the old paper card you used to fill on the plane.

decision.title: Which do YOU need? (30-second check)
decision.intro: Find the row that matches you. Rules depend on nationality, so always confirm your own case at the official site.

branches.case: You're from one of the 22 K-ETA-exempt countries (US, UK, Japan, Canada, EU, Australia…)
branches.summary: Just do the free e-Arrival Card. That's it.

branches.case: You're visa-free but NOT on the exempt list
branches.summary: Get K-ETA (holding it exempts you from the e-Arrival Card).
Apply for a tourist visa at a Korean embassy first.

decision.legend: * Holding a valid K-ETA exempts you from the e-Arrival Card.

ketaSteps.title: How to apply for K-ETA — step by step
ketaSteps.note: Only if your nationality is not currently exempt. The official process on k-eta.go.kr has 7 steps and usually takes 10–15 minutes.

steps.title: Agree to the terms
steps.detail: Open k-eta.go.kr (or the official K-ETA app) and start a single or group application. Read and accept the terms.

steps.title: Verify your email
steps.detail: Register or verify with an email address. Your approval and receipt are sent here — use an address you can access while travelling.

steps.title: Enter passport info
steps.detail: Type your passport details (or scan the photo page). If you're exempt, a pop-up appears here telling you K-ETA isn't required.

steps.title: Fill the application
steps.detail: Add your trip details, address in Korea, and upload a passport-style face photo (plain background, no glasses/hat).

steps.title: Review everything
steps.detail: Double-check name spelling and passport number against your actual passport — mismatches are the #1 cause of problems at the gate.

steps.title: Pay the fee
steps.detail: Pay ₩10,000 by card. This fee is non-refundable, even if the application is later declined.

steps.title: Get approval
steps.detail: Most approvals arrive within minutes, but it can take up to 72 hours. Save the PDF/screenshot; airlines may check it before boarding.

prepare.title: Have these ready before you start

items.d: Valid for your whole stay. You'll enter the number exactly as printed.
Passport-style: plain light background, face clearly visible, no glasses or headwear.
Approval and receipt are emailed here.
For the ₩10,000 fee (K-ETA) — the e-Arrival Card is free.
Your first hotel/stay address and phone are asked on both forms.

earrival.title: The e-Arrival Card (free) — don't skip this
earrival.intro: Since 2025, Korea replaced the paper arrival card with a digital e-Arrival Card. Almost every short-term visitor files it — the big exception is people who hold a valid K-ETA (and registered residents).

steps.title: Open the official site
steps.detail: Go to e-arrivalcard.go.kr — it's free. Beware paid look-alike sites.

steps.title: File within 72 hours of arrival
steps.detail: You can only submit within 3 days of landing (Korea time). Filing too early means it expires before you arrive.

steps.title: Enter passport, flight & address
steps.detail: Passport info, flight number, and where you'll stay in Korea.

steps.title: Save the confirmation
steps.detail: Show the QR/confirmation at immigration to skip the paper queue.

exempt.title: K-ETA-exempt countries (through 31 Dec 2026)
exempt.intro: Citizens of these 22 countries/regions can currently enter without K-ETA. The waiver is scheduled to end and K-ETA returns on 1 Jan 2027 — reconfirm before you travel.

items.d: Third-party sites buy top search ads and charge US$40–50 for a free/₩10,000 government service. The only official sites are k-eta.go.kr and e-arrivalcard.go.kr.

items.t: Filing the e-Arrival Card too early
items.d: It expires 72 hours after you submit it. File it within 3 days of your flight, not weeks ahead.
Your name must match your passport exactly. A single wrong character can stop you at check-in.
Blurry photos, glasses, hats or busy backgrounds get bounced. Use a plain, well-lit passport-style shot.
The waiver is temporary (ends 2026-12-31) and the country list changes. Reconfirm your status close to travel.

items.q: I'm from the US / UK / Japan / EU. Do I need K-ETA?
items.a: Not right now — those are on the 22-country waiver through 31 Dec 2026, so you skip K-ETA and just file the free e-Arrival Card. This is scheduled to change on 1 Jan 2027.

items.q: Is K-ETA the same as a visa?
items.a: No. K-ETA is a travel authorization that lets you board and enter visa-free; it is not a visa. If your nationality isn't visa-free, you still need an actual visa from a Korean embassy.
Three years from approval, with multiple entries — so one approval usually covers repeat trips until it expires or your passport does.

items.q: How much does it cost and is it refundable?
items.a: ₩10,000 (about US$8). The fee is non-refundable, even if your application is declined.
At least 72 hours before boarding. Many approvals come within minutes, but leave a buffer in case yours is reviewed.

items.q: Do children and seniors need K-ETA?
items.a: Historically travelers 17 and under or 65 and over have been exempt from K-ETA. Confirm the current age rule at k-eta.go.kr before you rely on it.

items.q: What's the e-Arrival Card and do I really need it?
items.a: It's the digital version of the paper arrival card, filed free at e-arrivalcard.go.kr up to 72 hours before you land. Most short-term visitors need it; valid K-ETA holders and registered residents are exempt.
Only k-eta.go.kr (K-ETA) and e-arrivalcard.go.kr (arrival card). Anything charging a big 'service fee' is a third-party reseller, not the government.
